item.title: Re: The Macguffin
item.content:encoded:
MAJOR CHANGES

Well then, I know it’s been a while but I think I know what to do.

Earlier I said that the Foundation couldn’t aim this artifact. I’m changing that, they did weaponize it, for a time. The main thing I’m changing is the way it targets a villain. Instead of the locket having its own sense of right and wrong it targets someone the holder views as evil. The thing is, it targets anyone nearby that is evil enough, that’s always been how it works I’m just making it clear.

What I’m planning on adding is a program where the Foundation uses the locket to defeat some small GOIs. It works, for a time. Then during one attempt, the holder of the locket turns around and proceeds to attack the Foundation. Causing serious damage and even unseating a site administrator. After being interviewed the holder confesses that they’d been questioning the morality of the Foundation for some time but had never thought of doing anything about it. That’s when the Foundation realizes that no amount of psychology or loyalty tests can tell if someone truly, in their heart of hearts, believes the Foundation is good. So they discontinue the program.

item.title: Re: Carnivorous Tattoo
item.content:encoded:
The first four bullet points are fine, and make sense. I have a better understanding of how the scp functions, thank you.

it favors more exotic predators such as extinct ones as a means of attracting more prey since the more intricate a tattoo the more it would attract tattoo enthusiasts.

I still don't understand what you mean here. To clarify: for .e.g. a tattoo of a sabretooth tiger appears on the victim's skin, followed by more "extinct" predators? I don't get why this would "attract" tattoo enthusiasts though.

I think the problem is you're missing a target, or specifically, the scp is missing a goal. That's why I asked who is being targetted and why. If the main target of the scip is "Tattoo enthusiasts", then you have to justify this and come up with a more plausible mechanics of how this happens. If the target audience, on the other hand, are violent gangs (who just happen to be heavily tattooed), then ah… do you see how the motivations / goals of the scp changes? Perhaps the entity was murdered by a gang member in the past

You're close to a greenlight. I just need you to work out / decide on a few more details.

item.title: Re: Yet another time travel tale...(Seeking Greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Hi, author.

+ show block
– hide block

I have some major issues with this. Mainly, you seem intent on "porting" a skip concept to a tale without really providing a fresh perspective or appeal that can't be found in the original. I think you want the time travel angle to offer new ideas, but I don't see that working very well. Why would time travel be more interesting than watching the story through a play? In fact, this seems to undercut the original significantly, since part of the appeal of HKT is that it's a fictional play, and thus its effects are more mysterious. Setting the same plot in the real world past doesn't add anything, and indeed seems to make the idea more shallow.

I think it is possible to explore this skip's narrative in Tale form, but I do believe you would need to bring something more unique to the table for that to be viable.

Have a good day!

item.title: Re: -1
item.content:encoded:
Offering my two cents as the author, I believe you unfortunately misread the whole article.

So, the first point. It's not anomalous, you say. For context, this article takes place in 2022, two years after the bushfires have occurred. Safe to say, if thousands of koalas1 still disappear at that point, without any fires, that would be utterly anomalous, right? I mean, it's the symbol of Australia, and someone's bound to notice the fact that they're disappearing.

Plus, I don't think large, flying serpents are a species native to Australia, because if that's the case, then I would be saving up in order to ride on those. Second, koalas are cute, and I won't trade those for snakes.

Second, I'm not sure on your thoughts about the pacing. You say "greatly written" at the start but then dismiss my article's pacing and narrative as a joke.

Choose one - it's ok if you found the article unsatisfying, but I'm just really confused about what you said.

Additionally, all people I asked did not point out that my article was too sparse and unnaturally progressing, and I'm against the idea that environmental action against climate change is a joke, so I have my doubts on everything you said.

Lastly, the ending (Incident DROPBEAR) was crafted in order to suit the New Year. Look, I don't want to shoehorn drama, politics2 and angst into this whole thing just to reduce the possible "that's it?"moment, because that would detract from the whole koala and aboriginal culture angle.

Plus, I'm simply basing off the fact that Dreamtime is rooted in the concept of an everywhen - the fact that it is timeless, so I actually don't feel good about you saying that this is a joke.

Footnotes
1. You should also note that even those in zoos - safe from bushfires - disappeared.
2. Australian politics are a whole another level, and as a Filipino, I didn't dare touch on that deeply.

item.title: Re: Cognation
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for your response I do really appreciate the feedback. I'll try and answer your questions as much as I can.

+ Show Response
- Hide Response

First the blood is the base anomaly. The first type discovered. I didn't mention this part in the initial post (which may be why it's more confusing) but the non-linear time of the dimension effects the blood, meaning it cannot age. As well as the ability to suck humes out of an enviroment.

The second blood isn't really another type of the scp, it's more like state of it 'awakened'. the higher the hume level the dimension has the less nonlinear time is. This effects the blood's own ageless property, causing it to change and go 'bad'.

The overuse of classification is a mistake, especially the dimension and the additional instance within the dimension is unnecessary and I'm gonna rethink that part. Also the hard science SRA babble isn't the clearest way to get across what the SCP does.

As for the containment procedures housing the 'awakened' blood would have to be using SRAs in a distanced wing of a site. Any blood that becomes awakened in the field needs to be recovered asap.

Additionally the main theme I wish to hit is there in the title. Cognation, from cognate which can be defined in a number of ways:

  1. Related by blood; having a common ancestor.
  2. Related in origin, as certain words in genetically related languages descended from the same ancestral root; for example, English red and Sanskrit rudhirá meaning red, bloody.
  3. Related or analogous in nature, character, or function.

The critical theme is the relation by blood, in both a literal and metanarrative sense. Blood connecting the girls from 231, Anna Lang and Robert Scranton.

The article itself would act as a relation by blood. Of Robert Scranton and The Scarlet King.

As for the significance for the wider universe, the Foundation could have been feeding/creating one of it's most infamous antagonists, unknowingly or knowingly. By using one of their own doctors no less.

Kind of going for the idea the foundation is forced into a hard situation. As a result a mixture of desperation and necessity causes them to use the blood large scale to contain reality benders.

I hope this is helpful and that it explains a lot more.

item.title: New author need greenlight for idea
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery

Elevator Pitch:
1. To classify a new SCP found from a meteorite in Arizona.
2. This SCP is a class Euclid anomaly. It can be potentially harmful to humans but benefit other SCPs.
3. Documents the new SCPs origin and potential tie into other foundation members.
4. Is a physical manifestation of anti-matter.
5. This document also serves as a warning to other foundation members for what dangers lie may occur if humans have extended contact with this entity.

Central Narrative:
Hikers keep disappearing in Sedona Arizona. The foundation finds it is due to an SCP that “hatched” out of a meteorite that crashed down to earth. This entity is intangible and dangerous to humans after extended exposure to it, causing them to “disappear”. It has a limited radius of its effect. This entity is a sentient black fog. It could be potentially useful to the foundation as it seems to interact with other SCPs in a positive way. It also needs to stay contained, as without proper measure, moves sporadically.

Hook/Attention Grabber:
This SCP is unique in the sense that though it is as of now classified as a Euclid entity, with the right research, could potentially become a Thaumiel entity if used to enhance the abilities of other SCPs the foundation finds useful. It also has the potential to be a tie into how anti-matter can affect other SCPs and may further help to understand all SCPs abilities. Not much is known about anti-matter today which is why I think it would be cool to have an entity made of it to enhance the aspect of mystery.

Additional Notes:
I already wrote a rough draft for the SCP article, but I am a new writer, so I must have the idea greenlight before the draft. My main concern is if there is another SCP like this as I have not read every article. I also want to make sure that I leave a lot of information a mystery without being overly vague.

item.title: Forum Criticism Team - Captain Post
item.content:encoded:
Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note from whom and where you received them. If you would like to receive draft critique without going through the greenlighting process, please use the IRC chatrooms to request reviews.

Please note that greenlights are given on concepts, NOT full drafts.

item.title: Danger, SCP-999!
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama, Emotional, Mystery

Elevator Pitch: Mysterious robotic entity found in Sweden. A group of cultists known as "The Children of the Scarlet King" trying to awaken it. The entity is eventually awoken, and easily contained, and has no real threat… until it meets SCP-999.

Central Narrative: The entity has no previous memories. Its memories slowly come back in small chunks. It meets SCP-999 and compulsively attacks it for a reason it does not understand. It claims that SCP-999 wanted to hurt it and was trying to defend itself (which is completely absurd). The missing information comes back to the entity in shattered pieces, however one factor is concrete, someone known as "The King".

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Children of the Scarlet King awakening an entity that attempts to kill SCP-999.

Additional Notes: This SCP will have many, MANY updates with cross tests, interviews, and containment breaches in the future.

SCP-999 will not perish in any future cross tests, containment breaches, etc.

item.title: Re: Semi-Veil breaking Parawatch SCP idea
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the feedback. I would just like to clarify something:

The SCP's effect is simplistic. I wrote it to be simplistic and be no real trouble for the foundation to contain the frog itself. The story comes when the picture ends up online. I chose Parawatch because they would be the most likely people to recognize anomalies outside the anomalous community and the most likely to spread the picture both across their platform and the internet. Parawatch has not suddenly acquired anomalous technology or contacts with another group, but they are not idiots and have been show to have proper precaution when working with anomalous images before.

A group of believer in the anomalous, who have got their hands on an easily-demonstrable anomaly, who can easily convince other people of their cause by sending them a picture of the anomaly, who aren't localized, who are paranoid, who have no knowledge of the veil or why it exists and are primarily communicating and spreading using the internet.

That is a concrete threat to the veil and one that the foundation would have a hard time shutting down.

The comedy comes from watching them try.

I think it's Ethics. I believe the author, fieldstone, has some other tales about the Foundation being cast as a morally-gray organization.

I was thinking about putting some exploration logs in my article

I'm not sure the in-universe Foundation would find it pertinent to identify D-Class backgrounds for exploration logs, unless said backgrounds would make a difference in the testing protocol (a D-Class who is a former professional spelunker going into a cave-based anomaly, for example, compared to a D-Class with no experience whatsoever for the type of terrain being explored).

I thought that it would be necessary to add a little background information about the D-Class so that the readers can warm up to the character.

Unless that background info makes sense from the perspective of a researcher, don't include it. Remember, the in-universe Foundation has no need to make readers of a dry professional report "warm up" to individuals mentioned in logs. If you include character information, there needs to be a good reason in-universe for a researcher to have it.
